system.summary: Imperial Cipher of 1544-1554: a syllabary in which the base shape gives the consonant and a mark the vowel (one dot a, bar e, two dots i, o-loop o, p-tail u), with alphabet signs, double-letter signs and nulls. Clear words stand in the cipher as code words.

diacritics.note: Marks select the vowel. Signs with two dots below usually read as nulls inside words, but some carry their plain value (yglesia, romper, guerra on c.60r L12), so the rule is not settled.

system.doubled_letters: own signs for ll rr ss tt (key)
system.sibling_key: Imperial Cipher of 1544-1554 (Meister 1906 p.212; Bertomeu Masia 2009), pictured on Cryptiana
system.notes: distinct_symbols counts sign names given here, some of which are variants of one sign. The key image was read at low resolution and extended from the text by hand. Clear words in the cipher: Pollo (the Pope, inferred), mus/mms (para, by sense), inta, em, vela/bela, nerp, gien, et ud, tu; not explained by the key. Folded in on 14 Nov 2026: WAINUT's table (wainut/key.tsv, 160 rows, its own sign names; wainut/key_frozen_1547.tsv frozen before the Charles letters) with the code words dide Su Magestad, quod Embaxador, gaces Rey de Francia, em franceses, gien vuestra, mus para from the contemporary decipherments of Philip's letters. Code values settled on 14 Nov 2026: Pollo Papa, mus/mms para, inta Su Santidad, em Franceses, gien vuestra, saa Duque, nerp/nep Francia (sense; the letters of the code word are open). Open: vela/bela, et ud, tu.

prior_solution.where: Contemporary: slip c.29 (13 May), c.77 (23 Dec), the clerk's margin notes on c.64v (20 Nov) and c.50r (30 Sep). No decipherment of the 14 Nov letter was found. Bertomeu Masia 2009 studies the Parma and Piacenza cipher correspondence and was not seen; it may print some of these letters. WAINUT's search (3 Nov 2026): Calendar of State Papers Spain IX and Venice V and the Treccani DBI do not print the 14 Nov letter; Corpus documental de Carlos V vol. III, Druffel and the Simancas minutes not opened.

conditions.human_role: Gave the lead 1560 page, said 'solve that cipher', approved each continuation, then said to continue as far as possible and publish. No hints about the key or the content.
tools: PIL crops, numbered panels at about 7x
subagents for c.60r block 2, c.61r, c.61v, c.62r and the short passages

solution.what: Found lead 1560 (Estense, Modena, Karl V to Ferrante Gonzaga) on the site; paged the Lodovico search (nris=48&page=N) to get the 151 record ids, then pulled the IIIF manifests and page images with curl (width limit about 1800 px, so crops were cut at native size).

Cryptiana (Tomokiyo) lists the 1549 letters to Gonzaga under the Imperial Cipher of 1544-1554 (alphabet signs, syllables with vowel indicators, ll rr ss tt signs, 8 nulls) and gives Meister's and Bertomeu Masia's key tables as images; the key images were saved.
Cropped the 6 cipher lines of c.30r (13 May 1549) at 1.5x and read them sign by sign by eye. First pass assumed 8 lines and read marker-like shapes (ap, mo, no, lo) as separate letters.
Tried base number plus vowel marker and a consonant-skeleton model on the signs. Neither held for the sign letters; the shapes ap, mo, no, lo are signs of the key itself.

Cut the clear slip on c.29 (the contemporary decipherment of the cipher on c.30r) into 117 consonant+vowel units; line 1 of the cipher has 19 signs for 19 units, so the alignment is one sign per unit. Read sign by sign against Masia's key shapes, the hand ruling where they differ.

Lines 1-3 of c.30r (about 60 signs) read against the slip: y pe n se y s e n e s te me di o de do n de y / co mo se ha n de sa be r lo s di ne ro s pa ra la o bra y / ta (m) bi e n lo s ma te ri a le s po r que se ga ne. About 30 glyph values fixed, most confirmed by key and by repeats.

Applied the table to c.64v (20 Nov 1549), passage 2: ... cosa en Parma de nuestra parte, as the clerk's marginal note says; then passage 4 (ofender y ocupar en (es)ta ocasion el estado de la casa Farnesa por la vezindad que tiene con el), passage 5 (tentar en tal tiempo; paresciere otra cosa y diere occasion se podra facilmente hazer) and the end of passage 3 (a la iglesia).
Passage 1 (end of c.64r, first line of c.64v) uses signs with dots below, a second series not in the table; passage 3 before 'a la iglesia' and the first half of passage 2 not separated.

Each c.64v reading was compared with the later-hand marginal note beside it (a summary of the same passage); all four agree in wording. No independent check of the sign readings and no measured token percentage yet.
Line 4 of c.30r aligned with the c.29 slip; lines 5-6 viewed but not aligned sign by sign. The decryption file is the slip text.
Located the 30 Sep 1549 cipher block on c.50r (5 lines) and its clear margin summary (Prior of Lombardy, castle, Brissac); signs cut at 3x; no slip, and the table did not settle line 1, so not read.

30 Sep 1549 block on c.50r: line 3 reads ca-s-ti-ll-o de = 'castillo de' (the margin note's word castillo, the key's ll sign); the rest of the five lines has about 20 signs outside the table and was not read.

c.77 (23 Dec 1549) is the clear text of the first cipher passage of c.76r. Line 1 of that passage (12 signs) aligns unit for unit with so-b-re-lo-de-ni-ca-si-e-n-do-a; this confirms eight values from c.30r and c.64v and adds four. Lines 2-3 not yet separated sign by sign.

c.76r passage 1 lines 2-3 and passage 2 line 1 aligned with the clear text on c.77: 'aquella plaça de la importancia que es y estando ... el Prior de Lombardia' and 'al dicho Prior a cuenta de la dicha'. About 25 values confirmed on a third page; two stretches (ça, fuera della) not separated.

30 Sep 1549 c.50r, with the margin note in view: signs fit line 3 to 'que', line 4 with one extra sign, line 5 to 'de', and 'y aunque' in line 1. 'fuese tanto', 'Brissac' and lines 1-2 did not map. Fitted to the note, not a test.

Blind test on 14 Nov 1549, c.60r, no crib: line 2 gave 'do al particular de la determinacion con que' with one new value (d = r, in Masia's key); line 3 gave 'apuntar y (ca?)pitular con el', first half unread. About 40 signs, by eye.

14 Nov 1549 c.60r first block, no slip or note: 'y viniendo al particular de la determinacion con que quedava desde .. apuntar y capitular con el Duque Octavio sobre la empresa de Parma .. algunas de las consideraciones que .. para despues .. daros a entender nuestra intencion y voluntad'. 142 signs: 116 firm, 11 doubtful, 15 unread (counted from 14nov1549_60r_block1.tsv). New sign values were chosen by context, so not a controlled test.

14 Nov 1549 c.60r second block, no slip or note: line 1 'teniendo respeto al poco fundamento que', line 5 'dinero estando en desgracia del Pollo como por'; lines 2-4 and 6 partial; lines 7-12 not decoded. Not counted. Several values chosen by context.

Base shape carries the consonant and the mark the vowel (one dot a, two dots i, o-loop o, p-tail u, cross-bar e). Seen on c.60r; not rechecked on the earlier pages; x with stroke and L with one dot sit outside it.

Rule base = consonant, mark = vowel scored on c.30r and c.76r: 21 hits, 3 misses, 1 not viewed of 25, not blind. Masia's key rows show the same pattern and correct the bases for ne, nu, tra, b, s. The rule contradicts two block-1 readings, capitular and Parma, now unconfirmed.

Rebuilt the sign table from Masia's key (Tomokiyo's image) enlarged. Rechecked two signs at higher zoom: both were misreadings (8 with one dot = ca, L with a dot = ma), so capitular and Parma stand. Reread c.60r block 1: 142 signs: 132 with a value, 3 doubtful, 7 unread. Signs with dots below and bare m are not in the key.

c.60r second block reread with sign_table.tsv: lines 1-8 mostly run (para una empresa como la de Parma, assi por lo que se tiene conocido della, no haviendo alli otras tierras, desde donde la pueda haver); lines 9-12 fragments. Not counted. Values applied with context in view; gra withdrawn as key-supported.

c.60v lines 1-4: 'no seria .. que romper la guerra con la yglesia, teniendo Su Santidad como agora tiene a Parma en nombre della y no de la casa Ferne..'. 96 signs: 82 with a value, 5 doubtful, 9 unread (lines 1-4 of about 28). Context in view, and the c.64v notes were known while reading.

c.60v lines 5-10: 'en favor de Ottavio como esta a la ro(?) que se hara capitulando con el, pareceria que se quisie[.]sse [..]do(?) tener y a no sa(?)r [.] de(?) rea[.] por mejor que el [.] m pe ra(?) o bien da si(?) que teniendo nos e s(?) te y [.] gualmente en Parma y en P(?)la ze(?) ncia nunca havemos querido emprender hasta qui ninguna cosa por via de [.] gue...' 240 signs: 209 with a value, 18 doubtful, 13 unread (lines 1-10 of about 28). Lines 7-8 do not form sentences. Context in view. Level crops misread signs at line ends; recropped along the slope and corrected.

Signs with two dots below may be nulls: four cases on c.60v (quisie.sse, .gualmente, .guerra, .nombre) where the word runs without them. Conflicts with the earlier lead that they are the plain sign (contra, c.60r). Not tested.

c.60v lines 11-14: 'guerra a vierta, esta a la ro(?) que se verna a en [.] la que [.] car el derecho que se pretende nuestra parte, allende que, capitulandose con el dicho Ottavio y muriendo el Pollo, se vernia luego a las manos con vo[.] se sso r' 343 signs: 305 with a value, 23 doubtful, 15 unread (lines 1-14 of about 28). Context in view. Line 7 corrected to derecho from the same pair of signs in line 12.
Clear word Pollo in the cipher (c.60r, c.60v) taken as Pope Paul III from 'en desgracia del Pollo' and 'muriendo el Pollo'. Inference from context and the date of his death, not from the cipher.

c.60v lines 15-18: 'sin poder escusar de meter en [.] y [.]o la discussion del derecho pretendido por las partes y veniendose al [.] fin a [.] tarde dar recompensa a la yglesia en caso que se hallasse se [. . .] e l dere...' 441 signs: 394 with a value, 26 doubtful, 21 unread (lines 1-18 of about 28). Longest connected run so far; derecho recurs with the same signs in lines 7, 12, 16. Context in view.

c.60v lines 19-22: '[dere]cho de las dichas tierras e l [.] da que pretenderia por otra parte ratificacion por razon de lo capitulado con el, por donde verniamos a hallarse embaraçado y car[.]gado por ambas partes [)]' 535 signs: 482 with a value, 30 doubtful, 23 unread (lines 1-22 of about 28). Line 19 confirms derecho from line 18. Context in view.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 2959 tokens, 251 types, es-golden-age order 4: reading -1.96 per letter; random keys -3.993 (z 9.5); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.546 (mean -2.561, z 45.5); annealer on the real text -2.342. Verdict: pass.

Rest of the 14 Nov letter: c.60v lines 23-28 by the main session; c.61r, c.61v, c.62r and c.60r block 2 by subagents; 30 Sep, 13 May, 23 Dec and c.64r by a subagent. All signs in sign files: 3032 signs, 2780 with a value, 128 doubtful, 51 nulls, 25 clear words, 48 unread.
docs/_validate.py on validation.tsv against es-golden-age: see outcome.validation. One line of the subagents' work checked against its crop by the main session.

Web search for a printed text of the 14 Nov letter and for Bertomeu Masia. Found only the listing of her 2009 book on Parma and Piacenza in Granvelle's correspondence; its contents could not be read online.
c.64r last two lines: dropping signs with dots below as nulls does not give Spanish.

Issue #618 (Brice Dudout): the Simancas sheet AGS D/00203 no. 243 opened. It is a reconstruction made in 1866 by the archivist Nemesio Ruiz de Alday from deciphered letters of 1545 in Estado, Flandes, leg. 501, not a table of the period. Its code list gives Papa pollo, para mus, Su Santidad inta, Franceses em, Vuestra gien, Francia nec; all six frozen code words of targets/ferrante1549/key.tsv (from contemporary decipherments) have the same value on it. Five of the nine open code words of this target are settled or confirmed (16 of 21 uses); inta and em change from 'the Church' to Su Santidad and Franceses. vela/bela, et ud and tu stay open. Reading files, codes_open and read share not changed in this round.

WAINUT (second, independent reading; files in wainut/): Issue #618 (Brice Dudout): the Simancas sheet AGS D/00203 no. 243 (a reconstruction of 1866 from deciphered letters of 1545, not a period table) read from the public PDF and compared with key.tsv. The six frozen code words (dide, quod, gien, em, gaces, mus) and Pollo have the same value on it; inta is Su Santidad there (key.tsv: doubtful la Yglesia); Francia is nec (key.tsv: doubtful nep); vela is not on it. His rerun of check_marks.py (95.5% with repairs) is his own figure; verbatim stays 811 of 910. key.tsv and the reading unchanged. Noted: targets/gonzaga1549 reads the same letter of 14 Nov 1549.

The two readings of the 14 Nov 1549 letter compared (compare_readings.py): the project's (sign files, 2,536 signs) and WAINUT's (wainut/, 2,543 signs), made apart from separate transcriptions and tables. Sign level: 2,523 places aligned, 2,312 carry the same value (91.6%). Word level: 725 words are sure and the same in both, 25 more differ only in spelling or division, 8 sure words differ; 77 words sure in one reading stand with a mark in the other. Of the 33 differences between sure words 10 are settled (gratificacion, tratar de, constara estar, fin es que, si, si en, contra, hasta qui and three divisions) and 23 stay open (Ottavio / Octauio and remittimos / remictimos on one sign, tt or ct; de / no exchanged at five places; hallarse / hallarnos; procurar / de curar; four vowel marks). Tables: 124 of WAINUT's 160 key rows occur in the letter; at 93 the project's sign files have the same value at more than half the places; systematic differences: tt/ct, ff/f, R ra/gra, N p/pl, the de/no pair, ys. No image was opened for the comparison.

Code values carried into both readings: Pollo Papa, mus/mms para, inta Su Santidad, em Franceses, gien vuestra (Simancas reconstruction of 1866 and WAINUT's frozen key), saa Duque (the 1866 list, the gloss 'Duq octauio' on c.76r, the project's reading; it fills WAINUT's hole at A03), nerp/nep Francia (both readings by sense, the 1866 list has Francia as nec with an end mark). The project's reading file is changed; WAINUT's filed reading is not: the values are in 14nov1549_reading_wainut_codes.md. vela/bela, et ud and tu stay open.

One strict recount per document (sure words only; doubtful, repaired, proposed and unresolved words are holes). 14 Nov 1549: the project's reading 837 of 1,007 tokens (83.1%; 129 of the tokens are sign values that do not form words), WAINUT's 817 of 910 words (89.8%; 811 before the code words; WAINUT's own figure with repairs is 864 of 910, 94.9%). 13 May 45/45, 23 Dec 46/48, 30 Sep first passage 33/35, 20 Nov 49/65 (the project's sign readings, fitted to the contemporary decipherments). Philip (WAINUT, scripts/check_marks.py rerun here): c. 10r 75/80, c. 28r D-E 56/66, c. 26r 75/91. The earlier 93.4% of this entry was a share of signs given a value, not of words read. No document without a contemporary decipherment reaches 95%: the entry stays read in part.

WAINUT's blind held-out test rerun after the fold (wainut/scripts/score_blind.py key_frozen_1547.tsv): 30 Sep 1549, 408 signs, 0.728 of the decoded letters in order shared with the marginal decipherment and 0.595 in runs of 4+ (200 shuffled tables at most 0.420 / 0.532); 20 Nov 1549, 140 signs, 0.652 / 0.323 (shuffled at most 0.519 / 0.355): passes on 30 Sep, fails on runs of 4+ on 20 Nov, as WAINUT reported. outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The letters were matched to the Imperial Cipher of 1544-1554 and to Bertomeu Masia's reconstruction as pictured by Tomokiyo on Cryptiana. Its rule and sign table, extended from the text by hand, gave the 14 Nov letter, which has no decipherment. Folded in on 14 Nov 2026: WAINUT recovered a table for the same cipher apart, from the contemporary decipherments of Prince Philip's letters (c. 14r for c. 12r, c. 11 for cc. 9r-9v), froze it and read the 14 Nov letter with it (outcome.parts).

texts.label: 14 Nov 1549, cc.60r-62r: the project's reading
texts.summary: Charles V tells his governor of Milan not to make terms with Ottavio Farnese over Parma: Ottavio has no money or troops, and it would mean war with the Church, which holds Parma, and could drive the Pope to give it to Orazio Farnese. Gonzaga may act only in two cases, an Orsini stroke or Orazio's entry, and then with dissimulation.

reading_review.note: Coherent for most of its length, with holes; c.60v lines 7-8 and 23-27 do not form sentences. Self-review, no person.

texts.label: 20 Nov 1549, cc.64r-64v
texts.summary: After Paul III's death: five short cipher passages forbid any move on Parma during the vacancy of the see, or any war on the Church, and put off an attack on the Farnese. The clerk's margin notes give the same sense.

reading_review.note: Fitted to the clerk's notes; the signs at the ends of passages 4 and 5 are weak and c.64r is not read.

texts.label: 30 Sep 1549, c.50r (first of seven passages)
texts.summary: Someone is dealing with the Prior of Lombardy, castellan of the castle of Nice, so as to throw him out and put in Brissac. The clear margin note says the same in brief and was in view.

reading_review.note: One sentence, one unread sign; margin note in view.

texts.label: 13 May 1549, c.30r
texts.summary: Gonzaga is to work out where the money and materials for a work will come from, without letting the intention show. The slip c.29 is the contemporary decipherment.

texts.label: 23 Dec 1549, c.76r
texts.summary: On Nice and the Prior of Lombardy, who is sent money and told to go and live in the castle. c.77 is the contemporary decipherment.

reading_review.note: Aligned with the contemporary slip c.77.

texts.label: WAINUT's reading: Charles V to Ferrante Gonzaga, Brussels, 14 Nov 1549
texts.summary: Charles forbids Ferrante's plan to conclude terms with Ottavio Farnese over Parma, gives his reasons, and approves only a private settlement. Ferrante may act in two cases: if Camillo Orsini plays a trick and Parma leaves the Church's hands, or if Orazio or another enters Parma by a deal with France or otherwise, when he is to try to make himself master of the city with dexterity and dissimulation. Otherwise nothing is to be started.

reading_review.by: AI language-model agent (for WAINUT; a model reading, not a person), independent of the solver
reading_review.note: Read as sentences 3 Nov 2026. Read sentence by sentence, the Spanish holds together and the English follows it: Ottavio is unreliable, terms with him would weaken the imperial claim and lead to war with the Church, only a private settlement is approved, and Ferrante may act in two named cases. The Spanish is heavily normalised, with about 53 repaired words and 43 proposals in roughly 940 words. The holes are worst in the opening sentence ('[?somontado]' is left untranslated) and in one clause of the second paragraph ('de la tiene de donde sacar [...] ... si de las de la yglesia de [...]'), which does not make sense as it stands. The closing c. 62r fragment ('el uerano que [?uiene]' from 'ueso') is a loose snippet.

texts.label: WAINUT's reading: Philip to Ferrante Gonzaga, Valladolid, 4 Aug 1548, c. 10r
texts.summary: Philip approves what Ferrante writes on Genoa, refers him to a letter to Ambassador Figueroa, and asks for prompt news of the King of France's descent into Italy.

reading_review.by: AI language-model agent (for WAINUT; a model reading, not a person), independent of the solver
reading_review.note: Read as sentences 3 Nov 2026. There are two short sentences, and both read cleanly as Spanish and match the decryption with only minor letter repairs (Genoua, Figueroa). The weak spots are the proposal 'd'Alua' (from 'daalui') and '[?serla]' at the end of the second sentence, which is not clear Spanish. The English papers over it as 'it being so'.

texts.label: WAINUT's reading: Philip to Ferrante Gonzaga, Madrid, 24 Nov 1551, c. 28r
texts.summary: Thanks for the guard of Nice; the business of Siena seems to go well. Passage C, on Parma and the Mirandola, is covered by a marginal decipherment.

reading_review.by: AI language-model agent (for WAINUT; a model reading, not a person), independent of the solver
reading_review.note: Read as sentences 3 Nov 2026. Passages D and E (thanks for the guard of Nice; the Siena business seems to be going well) read as coherent Spanish. However, about 10 of the 66 words are repaired or proposed: 'guarda de Niça' from 'guardenica', 'damos' from 'dimos', '[?siempre]' from 'siende', '[?plaça]' from 'paca' and 'encamina' from 'encamana'. Passage C is translated from the margin and is not in the Spanish reading, though the decryption's C lines also decode it plainly. The text is short, so there is little context to check the proposals against.

texts.label: WAINUT's reading: Philip to Ferrante Gonzaga, Madrid, 24 Nov 1551, c. 26r
texts.summary: The Germans sent by the Emperor should help finish matters; thanks for a paper on Siena. The vicariate passage rests on broken words.

reading_review.by: AI language-model agent (for WAINUT; a model reading, not a person), independent of the solver
reading_review.note: Read as sentences 3 Nov 2026. This is the weakest of the four, but it is just coherent. The first sentence starts mid-thought, leaves the destination of the 'baxada' unread ('[T]'), and keeps 'condision' in the Spanish while the English renders it 'provision', a mismatch the reading does not explain. In the second sentence, the subject 'copia de la minuta del priuilegio del vicariato' is four stacked proposals from 'capaa', 'misuta', 'disulerio' and 'uicaraato'. 'priuilegio' is the shakiest of them. The rest of that sentence (thanks, 'embiarla', 'scriuo al obispo de Arras') reads well.

texts.label: WAINUT's reading: Charles V, 13 May 1549, c. 30r: covered by c. 29r

outcome.fraction_read_source: Strict recount of 14 Nov 2026 (compare_readings.py, comparison_summary.json), sure words only, per document, never pooled. fraction_read is the higher of the two readings of the 14 Nov 1549 letter: WAINUT's, 817 of 910 words (89.8%) after the settled code words (811 before; WAINUT's own figure with marked repairs 864 of 910, 94.9%). The project's reading of the same letter: 837 of 1,007 tokens (83.1%; 129 tokens are sign values that do not form words). The earlier figure of this entry, 93.4%, was a share of signs given a value. Other documents: 13 May 45/45, 23 Dec 46/48, 30 Sep first passage 33/35, 20 Nov 49/65 (project, fitted to the contemporary decipherments); Philip c. 10r 75/80 (93.8%), c. 28r D-E 56/66 (84.8%), c. 26r 75/91 (82.4%) (WAINUT, verbatim count).
